GREEN’S ARCTIC LAMPS FOR CANDLES.

IMPROVED PATENT.

In the new Arctic Lamps the shade support is stronger, having three
arms instead of two; the extinguisher is not so upright and will
not fall down if the lamp is moved. The fitting for candlesticks is
simpler and obviates any difficulty in removing the plug from the
candlestick nozzle.

A tapering adjustable rubber end is now made which will fit in any
size nozzle; it does not scratch silver, and is especially suitable
for china or glass candelabra.

The Arctic Lamp is constructed on the same principle as a carriage
or reading lamp, in which the candle, enclosed in metal tube, is
forced up as it burns by means of a spiral spring inside.

It fits in any candlestick, and is made to exactly resemble a wax
candle when in use.

For the dinner table decoration it is particularly useful, as the
candles remain the same height, yet are burnt to the very end
without the slightest waste.

No more guttering candles; no more candle shades taking fire; no
smoke or smell when extinguished.

A PUBLIC TELEPHONE IS PROVIDED IN THIS DEPARTMENT FOR CUSTOMERS’ USE.

list are subject to alteration without notice._

EXCEPTIONS TO GENERAL RULES OF CARRIAGE

Garden Furniture (Exclusive of Rollers, Mowers, etc.). Delivered
free to most stations in England if of the value of 45/0, exclusive
of packages. Also to Dublin, Belfast, Edinburgh, Glasgow, Isle of
Man, and Channel Islands, if of the value of £5 10s. 0d., exclusive
of packages. Goods for Isle of Wight carriage paid to Southampton if
of 45/0 value.

Wire Netting delivered free in lots of 70/0 to any station in
England and Wales direct from Works. Special prices for Ireland and
Scotland. Exact size of mesh cannot be guaranteed, but is the same
as accepted by the Trade.

WIRE NETTING IS NOT INCLUDED WITH OTHER GOODS CARRIAGE PAID, UNLESS
OF ABOVE VALUE.

Mats are charged cost price, and are not returnable.

Packing for Greenhouses, Summer-houses, Melon Frames, Plant
Preservers, Dog and Poultry Appliances, allowed two-thirds if
returned carriage paid and in good condition.

Sewing Machines.--Carriage paid on Sewing Machines under the value
of £2 to any Railway Station within 100 miles of Harrods. The
value of £3 and over to any Railway Station in England and Wales
and Channel Islands. Value £4 to any Railway Station in the United
Kingdom.

Cases allowed full price if returned carriage paid within one month,
with address of sender attached.

Lawn Mowers (Sent Direct from Makers). Carriage paid to principal
stations in England, Scotland and Ireland.

Wringing Machines, Portable Coppers and Washing Machines

Special terms for carriage given on application.

Carrier’s Sheet.--Customers are particularly requested, if unable
to examine Contents of Consignments at time of delivery, to sign
the Carrier’s Delivery Sheet “Not Examined,” so that claim on the
Carrier can be maintained should goods be damaged.

Empty Cases, etc., returned to Harrods should bear the name and
address of sender, and should also be advised by post.

Estimates Free

For goods to be made to order and all kinds of repairs, etc.
Harrods’ printed Estimate form only can be recognised.

A deposit of one quarter the estimated amount is required on any
article to be made to a Customer’s order, unless such customer has a
deposit account with Harrods.

Perambulators and Baby Carriages

Carriage paid if within the delivery radius of our own Carts. For
the Country, special prices will be quoted according to distance.

REPAIRS

Special attention is paid to all kinds of Repairs, goods being
called for and returned by our Carts, daily.

Estimates for the repair of Baths, Knife Machines, Mincing
Machines, and every kind of Household Machinery. A special feature
is made of the re-tinning of all kinds of Copper Goods, which can be
returned in many cases the same day.

A COMPETENT MAN WILL BE SENT TO TAKE INSTRUCTIONS FOR REPAIRS.

ALL ESTIMATES FREE.

A charge will be made for collecting and delivering Wringing,
Mangling, or Washing Machines, or any other heavy or exceptional
article sent for repairs, whether estimate be accepted or not.

NOTES.--

A.--The lean-to houses are made to suit walls with flat, true, or
even surfaces to lean against; any provision for projecting piers,
window openings, rain-water or drain pipes, &c., entails extra cost.
In no case is any lead flashing or fillet provided at back wall;
this is at purchaser’s expense.

B.--Every care is taken to prevent breakage of glass in transit,
and any glass broken will be replaced free of charge, provided the
packages are signed for on arrival as “not examined” or “damaged
in transit,” but we cannot hold ourselves responsible beyond the
replacement of breakages.

C.--If concrete foundations are preferred in place of creosoted
sleepers, they must be provided by purchaser from plans which we
would provide.

D.--It is always desirable to paint these houses one extra coat
after erection, as the paint is liable to be rubbed or otherwise
damaged in transit on rail and in handling when fixing.

Packing Cases are charged, but allowed for in full if returned
Carriage Paid.

HARRODS LTD. LONDON]

By the scientific construction of the “Harrod” Cabinet
Refrigerators, the consumption of ice is reduced to a minimum.
These Cabinets are unique in many ways, one distinct advantage
being the completely separate chamber for the ice, which is not
exposed to the outside or warm air when putting in or taking out
edibles; this obviates unnecessary waste, and renders these cabinets
both economical and efficient. They further commend themselves to
intending purchasers by their convincingly moderate price.

THE RATNER PATENT TWELVE-CORNER-BENT SOLID STEEL SAFES. Nos. 2 & 3.

Safes are delivered free of charge in London to customer’s house,
but should same be required to be hoisted or taken upstairs to
flats, &c., an extra charge will be made accordingly.

[Illustration]

FIRE AND FALL RESISTING.
These Safes are far superior to the ordinary Four-Corner-Bent Safes.
The body is bent out of one solid steel plate ¼ in. thick; Door ½
in. solid steel plate, strengthened to 1 in., drill-proof over Lock,
and secured by a Seven-Lever, Unpickable, Gunpowder and Drill-proof
Lock. The bodies are formed of one plate of steel bent at the twelve
corners, thus introducing the important feature of a body which in
no way depends upon screws or rivets. This improved construction
enables a Safe to withstand a much greater fall than a Safe made
in the usual way. The Fire-Resisting Chambers are 3½ inches thick
throughout.

JOINTLESS AT ALL TWELVE CORNERS. EXTRA STRONG.
Body made of tough steel ¼ in. thick, bent at twelve corners, the
back being securely riveted on the inner face of the back flange.
Doors ½ in. steel plate, strengthened to 1 in. over Lock and other
vital parts. Lock Case of steel, T section 3 × 2½ × ⅜ in., fitted
with numerous steel bolts in front and a continuous fixed bolt at
back of door. The door rabbets against a strong bar frame, entirely

Seven-Lever Unpickable Powder and Violence Proof Locks, protected by

fire-resisting chambers, 4 in. in thickness, filled with best
non-conducting composition, in which is mixed chemical material
evolving moisture on the application of heat.

Preston’s Patent Weed Extractor. 33 in. long. Weight, 1¼ lb. A
simple and effective implement for ridding lawns, bowling-greens
etc., of dandelions, daisy roots, etc. 2/11 each.

Place the cutting edge of barrel over the centre of the root or weed
and with a downward pressure, giving at the same time a turn of the
wrist. Upon withdrawing the cutter from the lawn a plug of soil
together with the root or weed will be found in the barrel; remove
this by means of the plunger, withdraw the weed from the plug of
soil, and the plug may then be replaced in the ground, so filling up
the hole made by the implement.

TOOL CABINET.

THE “COMPACTUM” TOOL CABINET.

This Cabinet is framed in dark American Walnut Wood, with Ash
Panels, and has a work bench made of very strong well-seasoned hard
wood, which is fitted with a patent Bench-stop, and also with an
improved iron Instantaneous Quick Grip Bench Vice. The fittings are
made of polished brass, and the Cabinet throughout is of superior
strength and workmanship. When closed it makes a handsome and
well-finished piece of furniture.

It is 3 ft. 6 ins. long × 2 ft. 6 ins. high; the top forms the
Carpenter’s Bench, which is 3 ft. 6 ins. long x 1 ft. 6 ins. wide.
An extension piece is sent out with each Cabinet; this can easily
be attached and firmly fixed to one end, thus making the Bench 5 ft.
long. In this respect it is a great improvement on any combined
Cabinet and Work Bench yet placed on the market. It can also be
fixed in front of the Bench for Wood Carving or for any other work
that requires a strong table.

[Illustration: THE “COMPACTUM” TOOL CABINET.]

An improved Combination Tool Cabinet. Joiner’s Bench and
Wood-Carver’s Table.

The above engraving shows the Cabinet with the extension attached to
it forming a full-size bench 5 ft. long. This engraving also shows
the Cabinet open, and it will be seen that the lower part is fitted
with racks or clips, in which to place the tools, and that the same
use is made of the inside of the two doors. There is also a back
to the Cabinet, which can be raised by an ingenious contrivance
with the greatest ease, and this is also used as a rack for tools,
so that “_each tool has its special position_.” The value of this
arrangement will be at once recognised by all methodical workmen.
Every tool will be in its proper place, and can be found when
required. On the right side of the Cabinet there is a cupboard to
hold the extension piece, and which can also be used to stow away
large planes or any other large tools that may be acquired. On the
left side are three drawers, as shown in the following engraving,
which will be found very useful for any additional tools, or for
small work of any description, and in front, under the bench, there
is a long shallow drawer, with partitions for nails, screws, brass
fittings, etc.

[Illustration: W M & S]

This engraving shows the Cabinet with the back lowered into position,
and the doors closed ready for use as a Joiner’s Bench, and fitted
with 2 in. Quick Grip Vice.

EXCEPTIONS TO GENERAL RULES OF CARRIAGE.

full price if returned, carriage paid, within one month._

_Packing SUMMER-HOUSES, WICKER CHAIRS, DOG & POULTRY APPLIANCES,
allowed two-thirds if returned, carriage paid, and in good condition._

 Signing Delivery Sheets. Customers are particularly requested, if

 this destroys all claim on the Carrier
 should goods be damaged.

 name and address of sender, and should
 also be advised by post.

HATHAWAY’S SHAKESPERIAN END OVER END ECCENTRIC MOTION CHURN

[Illustration: CHURN SHOWING GRANULATED BUTTER BUTTERMILK COPYRIGHT
HATHAWAY MAKER]

This celebrated Churn is entirely without beaters, the interior of
the Barrel being perfectly clean and smooth. The Butter is produced
by the sharp and continual concussion caused by the cream falling
from end to end, and comes in small granules, the grains of Butter
being separated from the milk or cream and kept separate from
each other until ready for making up. The whole of the Butter is
extracted from the milk or cream and can be churned, washed, salted,
and worked in the Churn without the application of the hand. The
Butter, as shown in the Granulated form in Churn, is ready to be
removed to the Butter Worker for making up.

BRADFORD’S NEW PATENT SINGLE-HANDLE FASTENER,

For “Diaphragm” and “Endundend” Churns.

Awarded Silver Medal, Royal Agricultural Society of England, 1910.

This New Patent Lid Fastener marks a further step towards
simplification and speed in fittings connected with barrel Churns,
one end of the barrel of which is formed by the lid of the Churn. A
rod, with a cam at either end, is attached to the lid, and when the
two swivel links which are attached to the Churn are placed over the
cam a single movement of the handle completes the fastening of the
lid and ensures a perfect and reliable joint. The lid is unfastened

WOOD ENGRAVING MACHINES AND PLATINUM POINTS.

[Illustration: No. T U 275. Round, Sharp. Standard A. 8/9]

[Illustration: No. T U 276. Flat. Standard A. 8/9]

Dark Shades of a very Soft Tint. 8/9]

[Illustration: No. T U 278. Flat. Extra Fine. 8/0]

[Illustration: M & C THE SIMPLEX]

The “Simplex” is so constructed that the Benzoline which is required
to keep the Platinum Point red-hot is utilized also for heating
the Point at first, thereby dispensing with the Spirit Lamp used
with the “Original.” The flame is blue and perfectly smokeless. By
turning the round Vulcanite Disc to certain marks, the Benzoline Gas
supplies the Lamp, or it may be directed, by a turn, into the heated
Point, and keeps this red-hot. By another turn, all escape from
the bottle is shut off, and this can now be safely packed away and
carried in any position.

The “Simplex” has a well-finished Nickeled Bottle. The “Simplex,”
with Standard “A” Point (No. 276) complete, 22/6 each. Extra Points
for the “Simplex,” 8/4 each.

[Illustration: No. T U 366. Improved Foot-Bellows. Constructed so
that the foot-board is raised automatically by the weight of the
heel. Further improvements have been made so that the bellows will
pass a greater supply of air than hitherto. With these improvements
they will be found useful to those who do much Poker Work, as they
leave both hands free. Price, complete 4/11 & 5/11]

[Illustration: ORIGINAL No. 3 M & C]

[Illustration: THE “PYRO” M & C]

The “Pyro” is a very handy machine, with an exceedingly simple flame
or burner-top. The flame-top, which takes the place of the Spirit
Lamp in the “Original” machines, is worked exactly like a gas jet,
and burns entirely without smell. The Platinum Point is the Standard
quality, as fitted to “Original” No. 2 or 3, and the “Simplex”
machine. The “Pyro” machine comes cheaper than the “Simplex” on
account of the simplicity of the flame-top.

The “Pyro,” complete with Standard “A” Point (No. 276), 16/10 each.
Extra Points, 8/4 each.

fit any of the Glass Bottles supplied with our machines. Price 1/11½
each.

 ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING DEPARTMENT.

MAINTENANCE.

The undeniable advantages to be derived from having Installation
always under the care of an experienced electrician are so obvious
that it is unnecessary to further comment upon them; Harrods wish
to impress upon their customers that they have made the Maintenance
of existing Electric Light Installations a very special feature of
their business.

In consideration of a small fixed annual charge they are prepared
to assume the entire maintenance of an Installation:--To replace
all broken or worn-out Incandescent Lamps; to replace or repair all
damaged or broken Shades, Switches, Fuses, Plugs, etc., etc.; to
make personal periodical surveys and examinations, and generally to
guarantee keeping the entire Installation in efficient working order.

A representative will be pleased to wait upon customers at any time
and to submit estimates of charges for this class of work.

Harrods are also prepared to undertake the entire Maintenance of Arc
Lamps, which includes the Cleaning and Trimming of same, as and when
required.

Estimates given for all kinds of Electrical work on the shortest
notice.

[Illustration: THE NEW EAGLE PORTABLE RANGE.]

This new Portable Range is of a distinct and improved type in which
are embodied several notable features and advantages. The Ovens
are exceptionally large and thoroughly ventilated, and can be very
quickly heated with the smallest quantity of fuel.

The simplest one movement of the poker converts the fire from
closed to open. The Oven and Boiler Dampers are combined into one
Self-indicating Damper, showing by the position of letters whether
the heat is on the Oven or Boiler only or both together.

A Draught Regulator is provided in the Hood, which can be regulated
to check the too rapid working and overheating of the Range. This
is automatically closed when an open fire is made. Improved Side
Boiler. No danger of cracking or burning out. All wearing parts are
interchangeable and easily replaced.

HAND POWER PASSENGER LIFT.

[Illustration]

Lifts for raising Invalids are often made on the hand power
principle. The Gearing is of amply strong spur wheel and pinion
type, machined V wheels for the ropes, and a powerful band brake.
All the wheels are securely fitted to steel shafts running in
suitable bearings. One hemp or manilla rope is usually used for
suspending the cage, and the guides are of well seasoned wood,
carefully prepared and jointed. The Cage can of course be made
in any design, but unless specially ordered consists of American
whitewood, V jointed, stained and varnished; but if required it can
be made of a design similar to illustration in mahogany or oak at an
increased expenditure. The Lift is hauled up and down by an endless
rope, and the brake cord is arranged close at hand for applying as
required.

 ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING DEPARTMENT.

COUNTRY HOUSE LIGHTING.

[Illustration]

AIR GAS LIGHTING.

An excellent method of lighting Country Houses is by Air Gas, which
is becoming very popular on account of low first cost, small upkeep,
and the general satisfaction obtained from its use. Air Gas can
be made available for illuminating establishments of all sizes,
and especially those of moderate dimensions, being quite simple in
manufacture and free from risk of explosion. Harrods have tested
every make of machine in the market, and can strongly recommend
Cox’s system. These machines are low in price but excellently made.

A 30-light machine can be run at its full capacity upon one gallon
of petrol for 4½ hours, each light giving about 100 c.p. It should
be understood that each light can, on all plants, be subdivided into
lights of less candle-power.

 ACETYLENE (GAS) FOR COUNTRY HOUSES.

We undertake the installation of complete ACETYLENE plants, and send
an expert to advise Clients or give an estimate for work required to
be done.

The ACETYLENE FLAME is peculiar and good in its affording a light
more like that given by the sun (daylight) than any other artificial
light; both colours and tints can be readily matched, and pictures
can be appreciated by it. No other artificial light has this quality.

The products of combustion are the same as from coal gas, but only
about one-twelfth the volume for a given light. The Acetylene flame
is quite smokeless.

It is a safe light, Acetylene being less poisonous than coal gas.
As the issue from an open burner is so small, it would have to be
left open for a very long period in a closed room to render the air
dangerous to breathe. The slow issue of gas is also an element of
safety against explosion, for a burner would require to be left open
several days to make an explosive mixture in a room.

[Illustration]

A good and reliable Generator is of course necessary to ensure the
foregoing.

New piping, if required, is inexpensive, as it only needs to
be one-third the size of piping for coal gas. Small pipes are
inconspicuous when run in finished rooms.

The Generator here illustrated is the Cavendish “A.B.C.”
(automatic), and is considered the most simple and economical
now before the public. The attention needed that of a lad or odd
man, is not more than ten minutes daily, and much less than the
time required by lamps. There are no mechanical parts except two
water taps, and nothing to get out of order or readily wear out.
The generating apparatus consists of the central gas holder, on
each side of which is a generating chamber and a condenser. The
generating chambers are in duplicate and work independently, which
is a great advantage in admitting of re-charging always being done
in daylight without wasting unspent material. The gas given is cool
and clean. There is no compression of gas or variable pressure from
the holder. There is a positive working escape pipe if the holders
should be carelessly over-charged. The Insurance Companies charge no
extra premiums where this Generator is used.

ELECTRIC LIGHTING FOR COUNTRY HOUSES, ETC.

[Illustration: PLANT ON VIEW IN OUR SHOWROOM.]

HARRODS’ ELECTRIC LIGHTING SETS are suitable for Private Houses,
Hotels, Offices, Public Buildings, Works, Railway Stations, etc.

Perfect Safety--Absolute Reliability--Simple--Compact--No skilled
labour--Automatic lubrication and switch gear--Runs for hours
without attention on Common Paraffin, costs less than half
Petrol--No smell, no noise, no vibration.

HARRODS’ SETS consist of: “Rational” Patent oil engine and dynamo,
switchboard, pipes and water tank, as above. Complete with Battery.

The capacities given are the actual number of lights which the
Battery can light for six and ten hours respectively; if the lamps
are lighted direct from the dynamo the ten hours’ capacity can be
considerably increased. The lamps are metal filament at 1 watt per
candle power.

A cheaper set can be supplied, driven by Vertical Engine. Prices on
application.

Current can be supplied at 2·4d. per Board of Trade unit (this
includes depreciation, fuel, wages, and stores).

In designing the sets it has been borne in mind that they will not
be operated by a skilled mechanic, but probably by a gardener or
handy man. Everything, therefore, has been constructed with the
object of making the whole plant simple and yet absolutely reliable.

Cheaper sets can be supplied if desired, but the results of a
long experience prove that the set illustrated can be thoroughly
recommended in every way.

How Harrods’ Electric Light compares in cost with other forms of
lighting.

HEATING AND COOKING BY ELECTRICITY.

[Illustration: THE HARRODIAN ELECTRIC COOKING STOVE.]

  The Silent Servant.
  This Stove has revolutionized the art of cookery.
  No attention required.
  Price, complete, £21.
  Full particulars on application.

[Illustration: No. E L 1279.]

Ferranti Electric Disc Stove for boiling, grilling, and toasting.

Very popular because of its general usefulness and portability.
It will accomplish all the work usually done on a gas ring, with
greater cleanliness and economy. Scientifically designed so that
no heat is wasted. The best results are obtained with clean
flat-bottomed utensils. An extension plate to allow two or three
utensils to be used at one time, together with silver grill and
toaster, may be obtained in Harrods’ Electrical Showrooms.

Single Heat Disc Stoves (for voltages up to 250 volts): Diameter
of top plate, 7 in.; weight of complete stove, 6½ lbs.; current
consumption, 700-800 volts; cost per hour (electricity at 1d. per
unit), ¾d.; time required (stove hot) to boil 1½ pints of water, 7
minutes.

Price (including connector and 9 feet of flexible cord), 32/0

[Illustration: No. E L 1280.]

Ferranti Electric Duplex Disc Stove for boiling, simmering,
toasting, and baking.

This apparatus forms the basis of a complete kitchen equipment.

The Heating Discs are extremely useful for many culinary
operations, and are made flush with the main plate so that several
utensils can be placed half on for simmering on the low heat. Each
disc can be switched on separately and regulated high or low, thus
providing five ranges of heat in the oven, viz.:--1 disc low, 200
watts; 2 discs low, 400 watts; 1 disc high, 800 watts; 1 disc high
and 1 disc low, 1000 watts; 2 discs high, 1600 watts. The frame
is of cast iron, well enamelled, with nickelled edges. The whole
apparatus is strong enough for rough kitchen use and yet well
finished to encourage cleanliness and care. The electrical gear is
extremely simple and reliable, and well protected in every way.
Length, 25 in.; breadth 18 in.; weight approximately, 100 lbs. Each
disc has a maximum capacity of 800 watts on the high heat and 200
watts on the low heat.

Harrods are famed for the quality of their Groceries and Provisions,
and regularly execute orders for customers in all parts of
the Kingdom. They also purvey for Clubs, Hotels, and similar
institutions, as well as for Yachts, House Boats, Camps, &c.

Weekly Price Lists giving the latest prices of comestibles are
issued each week, and afford practical assistance in the selection
of requirements.

An inspection of the Food-Stuff Departments cannot fail to impress
the visitor with the absolute cleanliness and the strict adherence
to hygienic principles which prevails everywhere.


 [Illustration: HLD GROCERY DEPARTMENT HLD]

A PUBLIC TELEPHONE IS PROVIDED IN THIS DEPARTMENT FOR CUSTOMERS’ USE.

GROCERIES, ITALIAN GOODS, FRENCH AND CALIFORNIAN DESSERT FRUITS, Etc.

Harrods will be glad if _Orders for each Department are made out
separately_, as it facilitates the execution thereof.

Town Customers are respectfully solicited to order _a Week’s supply
of Groceries_, as it minimises the cost of distribution and enables
us to reduce prices still further.

All bottles of Sauces, &c., are designated as ¼ bottles, ½ bottles,
and bottles, instead of ½ pints, pints and quarts, in consequence
of the New Weights and Measures Act, and all Tinned Goods about the
specified weights.

Great care should be observed in unpacking Groceries, etc., as many
instances occur daily of articles being found in Cases returned to
Harrods as empty.

Customers will oblige and facilitate the execution and despatch
of Orders by kindly affixing prices, kind and quantity of article
required, and not to order _“same as before”_ as this entails
reference and consequently delay.

Customers will kindly note that in executing Orders for Goods not
appearing in Catalogue _some delay may occur_; although, of course,
the Directors will see that the Orders are executed with the
greatest possible rapidity.

The following Prices are subject to _Fluctuations of the Market_.
Alterations and additions are published in “Weekly Price List,” post
free on application. _Special Supplementary Lists are issued when
necessary._

Any article not quoted in list which has to be procured, will be
sent carriage forward.

 BISCUITS.

McVITIE & PRICE’S Biscuits, Edinburgh.--We desire to call attention
to McVitie & Price’s Oatcakes and Biscuits, which are of excellent
Quality.

_Huntley & Palmer’s, Macfarlane, Lang & Co.’s, Peek, Frean & Co.’s,
and other Makers._

Customers will oblige by stating whose Make they require.

Huntley & Palmer’s, McVitie & Co.’s, Peek, Frean & Co.’s, Macfarlane
& Co.’s and Jacob & Co.’s tins charged 0/8 each, Crawford & Co.’s
0/6 each, and the same allowed when returned in good condition.
Small tins are included in the following quotations, and allowed for
when returned in good condition, as per list.

Any Biscuits of the above Makers can be supplied, but those not
named in the List will take a few days to procure.

The Biscuits are guaranteed to be sent out in sound condition,
and no allowance can therefore be made for breakages in transit.
Customers are strongly recommended to order all Biscuits in tins,
thereby preserving their flavour and crispness for a considerable
period.

Customers are respectfully asked, before signing for Drum, Can, or
Cask, to make certain that it is in a perfect condition and not
leaking, as the Company do not hold themselves responsible for any
loss after the cans and casks have been accepted and signed for
by the Railway Companies and Carriers; and customers residing in
London are recommended not to order these Oils in casks, as the
difficulty the carriers experience in delivering them down area
steps or underground cellars renders the casks liable to leakage,
which cannot always be stopped in time to prevent loss. Any that are
delivered will be at Consignee’s own risk.

Complaints are frequently received of the quality of the oil
supplied, but, upon investigation, it is found in nearly every
case that the lamp is in fault. Customers making use of Kerosene
or Crystal Oil for lamps are recommended to observe the following
precautions. By so doing the liability to explosion will be avoided,
and the best light obtained.

No lamp should be used in which there is a possibility of the oil
coming into contact with the flame. The well should not be filled
too full.

When a lamp has been unused for a considerable time, the well should
be drained and the whole thoroughly cleaned, filled with fresh oil,
and fitted with a fresh dry wick.

Special attention should be paid to the size and quality of the
wick, which should exactly fit the burner (so as to move up and down
easily, but not loosely), and should be of soft texture, and not too
highly plaited.

When putting out a lamp, care should be taken not to screw down the
wick low enough to allow any of the charred portion to fall into the
well.

The lamp should not be blown out, but the wick should be turned down
very low and left to go out.

Mineral Oils are accepted by Railway Companies on the days specified
below, and all orders should reach the Stores on the day previous to
ensure dispatch.

 Turtle Soup Tablets ...  ...  ...  ...  per box of 4 tablets 1/0

Each tablet contains a considerable proportion of real Turtle, and
makes a large cup of nourishing food.

Directions for Turtle Soup.--The preparation requires to be soaked
in cold water for three days (changing the water daily), when it
extends to three or four times its present bulk or weight--becoming
exactly similar to the Calipash and Calipee obtained from the fish
after being killed. It is then to be cut into pieces of about an
inch square, added to a suitable stock, and cooked until quite
tender. One pound weight of Dried Turtle is sufficient for three
quarts of soup. A glass of dry sherry added to each quart of soup
will be found an improvement. Lemon juice and cayenne to taste.

WHAT IS SAPOLIO?

It is a solid, handsome cake of scouring soap, which has no equal
for all cleaning purposes except the Laundry.

To use it is to value it.

Sapolio To Brighten Metals.

Sapolio To Clean Dishes.

Sapolio To Scour Bath-tubs.

Sapolio To Renovate Painted Work.

_WHAT WILL SAPOLIO DO?_

Why, it will clean paint, make oilcloths bright, and give the
floors, tables and shelves a new appearance.

It will take the grease off the dishes and off the pots and pans.

You can scour the knives and forks with it, and make the tin things
shine brightly.

The wash-basin, the bath-tub, even the greasy kitchen sink, will be
as clean as a new pin if you use SAPOLIO.

One cake will prove all we say. Be a sensible housekeeper and try it.

Many articles pretend to do the work of SAPOLIO. They are good after
their kind, but, well--JUST TRY SAPOLIO.

A small bowl of Water, a cake of SAPOLIO and a cloth will do more
cleaning than a pail of water and three cakes of ordinary soap.

Sapolio To Scour Kettles.

Sapolio Saves Time.

Sapolio Lessens Labour.

Sapolio Does the Work Better!

  _Highest-Class Caterers and_

This Department is fully equipped with all modern appliances for
the carrying out of Society Functions and Entertainments, such as:
Dance and Hunt Ball Suppers, Coming of Age Festivities, Theatre
Suppers, Private and Public Luncheons, Dinners, Wedding, Afternoon
and Evening Receptions, Garden and Children’s Parties, Military Race
Meeting Luncheons and Teas, etc.

Experts sent to any address (Town or Country) to estimate and give
full particulars.

Chefs, Cooks, Menservants, Waiters, Parlour Maids, Waitresses, sent
on shortest notice, Town or Country.

All Contracts undertaken by us are carried out by a well-trained and
thoroughly reliable Staff.

Estimates given for any Function.

 BAKERY DEPARTMENT

WEDDING CAKES.

Harrods have gained special distinction in this Branch, and supply
exclusive and artistic Cakes from 10/6 to 50 guineas each at the
uniform price of 1/6 per pound. Harrods make all their Cakes on the
premises in their own bakery, and employ for this work only the most
skilful and successful English and Continental Specialists. They
supply one standard quality of cake only, the choicest that can be
made, and of delicious quality and all-round excellence. The Cakes
are encrusted with a thick layer of pure Almond Paste, artistically
iced and piped with white sugar, which is made by a new process
rendering it EASILY cut (not the usual hard icing), handsomely
ornamented with silver decorations, etc. They are sold by weight at
1/6 per pound, unless otherwise arranged, and this price includes
a finished Cake with simple decorations. Top centre ornaments and
fuller decorations extra. Cakes intended to be decorated with
natural flowers, and on request, are suitably piped to admit of
this. To enhance the appearance of Cakes, a silver stand and saw
can be hired at a nominal price, according to size; and, unless
specially instructed to cut in wedges, all Cakes are sent out intact.

CUT WEDDING CAKE, finest quality almond, iced, any weight per lb. 1/6

Prices for supplying Boxes and Packing:--Per doz. boxes--Customers
supply Cake--3/6¼ lb., 4/0½ lb. Harrods supply Cake--6/6¼ lb., 12/0½ lb.

Prices for supplying Boxes, Packing, Addressing, and including
Postal Charges (Inland):-- Per doz. boxes--Customers supply
Cake--5/6¼ lb., 7/6½ lb. Harrods supply Cake--8/6¼ lb., 15/6½ lb.

Packing and Delivery.--Great care is used in packing and delivery of
Wedding Cakes; customers may rely upon them arriving in good time
and condition. It is desirable, where possible, to give a reasonable
length of time in order to admit of the Cakes receiving proper
attention. Urgent orders will, however, be executed as expeditiously
as possible. For special illustrated list of Bride Cakes, Ornaments,
&c, see following pages.

Wedding Cakes for Export.--The high standard of quality which

NOTES CONCERNING ICES, Etc.

_Directions for turning out and serving sent with all Ices._

BY-THE-QUART ICES, sent out in Freezers, specially recommended for
keeping frozen the longest time. One quart is considered sufficient
for twelve persons.

ICES IN MOULDS AND ICE PUDDINGS, delivered in moulds. When ordering
please state the shape of mould required, whether “tall” or “flat
fruit-top” shape.

FANCY FRUIT DESSERT AND NEAPOLITAN ICES, supplied in moulds or
in turned-out form on Laced Papers in Freezers. Unless otherwise
ordered, these Ices are sent out in mould. Sugar Leaves for serving
Fruit Ices on, made to order, price 4/0 per doz.

ICED COFFEE, CHOCOLATE AND SORBET sent out in Freezers.

ICED SOUFFLETS, supplied in suitable dishes, and delivered in Ice
Caves.

For the convenience of customers, experienced men are despatched to
any address for the purpose of turning out and serving Ices at a
charge of 2/6 per hour, travelling expenses extra.

MERINGUES, being of an exceedingly fragile nature, are sent out at
customer’s exclusive risk, and no allowance for breakages can be
entertained.

UTENSILS are collected the day following delivery. If kept longer a
charge for hire will be made. No deposit for same is required unless
delivered outside radius of our own van deliveries.

Cellar Temperature. It should be dry and well-ventilated, not
draughty; temperature not to be below 50° Fahr. nor exceed 60°
Fahr. All Wines binned away on their side (Port with chalk mark
uppermost). Crusted Wines should be decanted before using. When
bottles are uncorked it is essential to wipe neck of bottle.

RECIPES FOR WINE CUP, CYDER CUP AND COCKTAILS.

CLARET.--To 2 bottles Claret add 3 bottles Soda Water, a liqueur
glass of Sherry or Orange Curaçao, the peel of a Lemon, powdered
Sugar to taste, a few slices Cucumber Peel, or, instead, some sprigs
of Borage.

CHAMPAGNE.--To each bottle Champagne add 2 bottles Soda Water, a
liqueur glass Orange Curaçao, a few slices Cucumber Peel (Maraschino
may be substituted for Curaçao).

CYDER CUP.--To each bottle Cyder add 2 bottles Soda Water, a wine
glass Brandy, and the peel of a Lemon with a sprig of Borage. A
small amount of Sugar to be added to taste, if a dry Cyder.

When the above Cups are completed, they should be put on the ice,
but on no account should ice be put into the cup.

MANHATTAN COCKTAIL.--Half fill a tumbler with chipped ice, add 4
drops Angostura Bitters, half a wine glass Scotch Whisky, half a
wine glass of Italian Vermouth, half a glass Curaçao, half a liqueur
glass plain Syrup, well shake, put in a piece of Lemon, and serve.

BRANDY COCKTAIL.--Half fill a tumbler with chipped ice, add 4 drops
Angostura Bitters, 1 wine glass Brandy, half a wine glass Curaçao,
half of Syrup, well shake, put in a small piece of Lemon, and serve.

Empties allowed for as follows: BOTTLES.--Champagne, 3d. doz.; Port,
Sherry, Brandy, etc., 6d. doz.; Whisky (White and Black), 9d. doz.;
Claret, 6d. doz. JARS.--½ Gallon, 1/6; 1 Gallon, 2/-; and 2 Gallon,
4/-. CASKS.--4 Gallon, 4/-; Octaves, 10/-; Quarter Cask, 15/-.

 The Renowned Scotch Whisky of Great Age.

[Illustration: Special Reserve Scotch Whisky V.O.H Special Reserve
Scotch Whisky OF GREAT AGE Blended & Bottled by HARROD’S Ltd.
LONDON, S.W.]

V.O.H. Special Reserve, of Great AGE.

Has the peculiar but most pleasing palatable flavour which is a
result of being matured in wood for a considerable number of years.
It is imbued with those exhilarating properties which stimulate the
brain to healthy activity, and it will appeal to connoisseurs as
being a Scotch Whisky in its truest Essence and Spirit.

V.O.H.

These Whiskies, which are the property of Messrs. Harrods, will at
once appeal to connoisseurs as rich and mellow blends of exceptional
purity. They are supplied to a large clientele, who prefer them to
Whiskies quoted at much higher figures because of their absolute
uniformity in quality, a feature so often lacking with many at the
same price. Harrods have never less than 3,000 gallons in stock
maturing in the wood, and they guarantee every bottle of their
V.O.H. Special Blend 8 years old, and their V.O.H. Reserve a Whisky
of much greater age.

Harrods highly recommend these two Blends to discriminating critics
who desire a genuine Old Highland Whisky, possessed of exhilarating
qualities without the detrimental after-effects associated with the
ordinary run of spirits.

 MINERAL WATER DEPARTMENT.

HARRODS’ MINERAL WATERS are manufactured in their own factory under
expert supervision. The greatest care is taken in the filtration
of the water prior to its aeration, every drop of water is passed
through a Pasteur (Chamberland) Filter, ensuring absolute purity.

Customers will please note that all sparkling waters should be kept
in a cool place.

Cases are charged as follows:--Harrods’: ½ doz., 1 doz., 2 doz., 1
doz. syphons and 3 doz. crate, 1/6 each. Schweppes’: Syphon cases,
3/6 each (returnable). Same allowed if returned in good condition.

The following are delivered to Railway Station, carriage paid, in
the following quantities:--Schweppes’ Mineral Waters, 3 doz. cases
bottles, 6 doz. cases bottles; 6 doz. cases splits; 1 doz. cases
syphons; Perrier Water, 100 cases splits, 100 cases pints, 50 cases
quarts; Harrods’ Ltd. Cyder, 4 doz. cases pints, 2 doz. cases
quarts; Burrow’s Malvern, 6 doz. cases.

_Note_.--The above Ales and Stout will be delivered free within the
London District. Allsopp’s and Bass’s Ales in Casks are delivered
free at any Railway Station in England. Guinness’s Stout and London
Stout in Cask are delivered free in the London district only.

For country orders casks are charged as following: Firkin, 6/0;
Kilderkin, 12/0; Barrel, 24/0; same allowed returned in good
condition.

Dublin Stout is per Irish Kilderkin and Firkin.

Bass’s or Allsopp’s Ales going to Scotland will be charged 1/0 per
Kilderkin and 2/0 per Barrel extra, thus rendering them delivered
free to any Railway Station.

For Ireland a charge will be made, payable on delivery, of 1/0 and
2/0.

 _Entertainment and Amusements Department._

[Illustration]

A PUBLIC TELEPHONE IS PROVIDED IN THIS DEPARTMENT FOR CUSTOMERS’ USE.

ENTERTAINMENTS FOR ALL OCCASIONS

All Entertainments booked at Harrods are subject to the following
conditions:--

1. No Entertainment booked can be cancelled or postponed unless half
the fee agreed upon be paid.

2. If postponed, the same Entertainment may be had within three
months at the remaining half fee, plus travelling expenses, provided
it can be arranged for at the time decided upon.

3. Travelling expenses are charged extra (to and from Harrods)
except when otherwise agreed upon at the time of booking.

advance as possible to allow of due preparation.

 Hire, Ball, Rout & Fête Furnishing Department.

HARRODS undertake and carry out contracts in any part of the United
Kingdom for Public Ceremonies, Decorating Public Buildings, Erection
of Triumphal Arches, Street Decorations, Public Illuminations,
Fireworks, etc., for National Rejoicings. Also for all kinds of
Entertainments, Bands, etc. The Erection of Pavilions of any
required size for Public Receptions, Weddings, Dances, Suppers,
Laying Foundations, etc.

ESTIMATES.

A representative will be sent to give quotations, offer suggestions,
and make arrangements free of charge within ten miles of London;
beyond that distance on payment of return railway fare, allowable if
estimate be accepted.


 GENERAL HIRE DEPARTMENT.

SUPPLY CUTLERY, PLATE, CHINA, GLASS, TABLING, etc., etc., ON HIRE,
SUBJECT TO THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS:--

No. 1.--Immediately upon delivery of goods the Customer becomes
 responsible for any loss or damage until they are again
 taken charge of by one of Harrods’ assistants.

No. 2.--That the accompanying Lists of Prices are fixed for one
 day’s Hire, the Goods being delivered on the day required
 for use and re-collected the day following. If the
 articles are to be re-collected the same day after use
 (necessitating special collection), an extra charge will be
 made. Should the Articles not be given up on application,
 additional Hiring will be charged.

No. 3.--That the goods may be Hired for any specified period, the
 charges being estimated, when the price is not specially
 given, in the following manner, viz.:--
 One day, as indicated in List.
 Two days, as one and a half days.
 One week, as twice one day.
 Two weeks, as three times one day.
 Three weeks, as three and a half times one day.
 One month, as four times one day.

No. 4.--That when Goods are conveyed by other than Harrods’ vans the
 Customer is responsible for any loss or damage during
 transit.

No. 5.--That when Goods are Hired for a term exceeding one week,
 Notice must be given to the Hire Department at least two
 days before the Goods are to be removed, otherwise
 Customers are responsible for such goods, and also for
 Hire for such time as they may be detained.

No. 6.--All Men servants engaged from Harrods are considered
 as servants of the Hirer, and the firm do not hold
 themselves responsible for any breakage or loss while
 these are in the Hirer’s employ.

No. 7.--Goods on Hire are not delivered free beyond our Town
 delivery, excepting small parcels, which will be sent free
 within our Suburban delivery, but an extra charge will be
 made for the delivery of bulky Goods. Carriage on Hired
 Goods sent to the Country will be extra.

Contracts undertaken in any part of the United Kingdom for
Decorating Public Buildings, Erecting Triumphal Arches, Illuminating
and Decorating Streets, etc.

FASHION DEPARTMENTS

 BABY LINEN
 BLOUSES

 DRESS MATERIALS
 FLOWERS AND FEATHERS

 LADIES’ BOOTS AND SHOES
 LADIES’ OUTFITTING
 LINENS
 MANCHESTER GOODS
 MANTLES
 MILLINERY
 SILKS
 TRIMMINGS
 UMBRELLAS


The Departments devoted to Fashion have a particular fascination,
the name Harrods being a _cachet_ with well-dressed people for
correct and distinctive attire.

Their fashion experts regularly visit the Continental markets. They
have established agencies in the leading centres which keep them
informed of the trend of fashion, and constantly feed them with
novelties.

Harrods have developed the manufacturing side of their fashion
business to such an extent that they now produce in their own
workrooms a great number of fashionable garments, including gowns,
coats, blouses, millinery, and underwear, many of original design as
well as replicas of selected Paris models.

This development of manufacture not only tends to improve quality
by giving Harrods the entire supervision of the materials and
workmanship, but also lessens the cost to customers, all middle
profit being obviated by this method of supplying direct.

 SILK DEPARTMENT.

SILKS, SATINS AND VELVETS.

Fashion demands a lavish use of these exquisite materials in every
lady’s toilette. Many and varied are the weaves stocked at Harrods.
The range of beautiful and artistic colours--many exclusively
dyed--surpasses any collection previously offered. Every shade
and tone that has a place in the present modes is stocked in many
qualities.

Not only in exclusiveness of material does Harrods’ supremacy lie;
their value also is never found lacking. The enormous output they
enjoy opens every market to them, so all French, Swiss and Japanese
silks are imported direct. The British silks also reach Harrods’
counters without the aid of the middleman, thus ensuring lowest
prices to Customers.

Why Harrods recommend  “Spunella”

THE fact that “Spunella” is included in Harrods’ stocks implies that
it has passed their test and attained the high standard of quality
required of everything sold by them.

“Spunella” is a pure silk fabric of British manufacture
throughout--is inexpensive, dainty, and useful, besides being a
fabric that washes and wears well; every colour is guaranteed fast
dye.

It is ideal for town or country wear, and is widely used for all
forms of sport. Write to Harrods for patterns of this excellent
fabric, a splendid selection posted free to all enquirers.

 DYEING & CLEANING DEPARTMENT

A PUBLIC TELEPHONE IS PROVIDED IN THIS DEPARTMENT FOR CUSTOMERS’ USE.

GENERAL INSTRUCTIONS.

HOW TO SEND GOODS.--Customers sending Goods for Cleaning or Dyeing
are particularly requested to enclose in the parcels their Name and
Address, with full particulars and instructions.

Parcels sent from the Country should always be advised per post, as
by so doing delay and miscarriage are prevented.

DELIVERY AND COLLECTION.--Goods are collected and delivered free in
London and Suburbs, but the articles must be in readiness, securely
tied up, to go by the carts when they call, as the large delivery
and collection of Goods will not permit of any delay. Name and
address should be enclosed in each parcel, also instructions.

NON-LIABILITY.--Harrods give notice that Goods are received only on
condition that they be not held responsible for loss arising from
any fault there may be in the material, and which is developed in
the process of dyeing or cleaning, or for shrinkage; every possible
care is exercised with goods which are faded and tender, but all
work undertaken at OWNER’s RISK.

CANNOT GUARANTEE.--Goods ordered to be dyed to match pattern the
exact shade cannot be guaranteed, but Harrods always dye as nearly
as possible to the shade selected.

 PRICE LIST.

The following prices have been carefully prepared, and may be taken
as a safe guide, although Harrods do not hold themselves bound to
them in all cases, owing to the immense variety in style and quality
of articles sent. A definite estimate can always be given before
putting work in hand, and quotations for quantities supplied on
application.

_All the above Finished by Special Machinery._

(For colours, see page 1501.)

 Glazing a Speciality.

Harrods have fitted up in this Department the most approved machines
for Polishing Dance Cloths, Carpet Covers, and Stair Damask.

They have also a special method for drying, which ensures perfect
freedom from Creases and an even surface.

Chintz Glazing is also a special study; and those requiring good
work at moderate charges would do well to give Harrods a trial.

CRETONNES, CHINTZES, and COTTON GOODS seldom clean successfully
by the CHEMICAL process. Harrods therefore claim to use their
discretion as to the methods most suitable.

The WHITE ground of CRETONNES and CHINTZES can be tinted with a very
pretty effect, and without changing the colour in the design. This
is an advantage where the colours are washed out or faded.

ORDINARY (or Wet) CLEANING is specially studied, as many articles
when stained or discoloured by wear can only be restored to anything
like their original condition by this method. A number of new
appliances enable Harrods to CLEAN and FINISH the work in a superior
manner.

able to dye Silk goods without unpicking or removing trimmings, and
by the adoption of this method the original lustre of the fabric is
maintained.

The result is an “Equal to New” appearance of such things as
Brocades, Satins, and Silks.

This method of treatment is particularly recommended for valuable
Ball and Evening Dresses, Silk Tea Gowns, Mantles and Costumes,
as it involves no risk of deterioration of material. Prices upon
application.

Important Improvement in Silk Finishing.

It cannot be too widely known that, after much patient experiment,
Harrods have designed and perfected a machine for softening
and imparting a clear surface and the original lustre and brilliance
to silks after dyeing.

Everyone knows the complaints so general about Dyed Silks--viz.,
that they are hard and papery, and have lost their former suppleness.
This can no longer be said about Silks, either for Dresses or for
Upholstery, dyed by Harrods.

N.B.--Owing to the use of chemicals in the production of many
Glacé and other makes of bright finished silks, the traces of which
cannot be detected before immersion, Harrods do not undertake any
risk in cleaning or dyeing; in all cases these goods are treated with the
greatest care to ensure a satisfactory result, but only at owner’s risk.

 Colour List.

The following list is correct generally, but as the desired colour
on some fabrics cannot always be produced, two colours should be
given in the order preferred, to save delay.

New shades are continually being introduced. Particulars on
application.

ANY COLOUR can be dyed Black. White can be dyed any colour.

Amber can be dyed Black, Brown, Claret, Dark Crimson, Dark Green,
Light Green, Scarlet, Light Brown, Olive, Cardinal and Peacock.

Black Satins, Silks, Velvets, Broadcloths, and Feathers cannot be
dyed any other colour, as they are generally fast.

Blue can be dyed Dark Brown, Green, Dark Mauve, Navy, Olive, Peacock
and Plum.

Blue (pale) can be dyed almost any colour.

Brown can be dyed Claret, Dark Green, Olive, Dark Prune.

Cardinal can be dyed Brown, Crimson, Claret, Myrtle Green, Navy,
Terra Cotta.

Claret can be dyed Brown, Maroon, Ruby, Prune, Dark Green, Olive.

Crimson can be dyed Brown, Cardinal, Claret, Green, Navy, Olive,
Prune, Terra Cotta.

Drab, Fawn and Grey can be dyed Blue, Brown, Cardinal, Claret,
Crimson, Green, Maroon, Mauve, Olive, Old Gold, Peacock, Prune,
Terra Cotta.

Green (dark) will dye Black, Brown, Claret, Dark Crimson, and Terra
Cotta.

Green (light) will dye Brown, Claret, Crimson, Maroon, Navy, Olive,
Peacock, Prune, Ruby, Terra Cotta.

Lavender will dye almost any colour except Amber, Light Blue
and Straw.

Maroon can be dyed same colours as Claret.

Mauve can be dyed Brown, Claret, Dark Green, Maroon, Navy, Olive

Navy can be dyed Dark Brown, Claret, Dark Green, Olive.

Olive can be dyed Brown, Claret, Dark Green, Maroon, Prune.

Peacock can be dyed Brown, Claret, Dark Green, Navy, Olive, Prune,
Terra Cotta.

Pink can be dyed any ordinary colour.

Prune can be dyed Brown, Claret, Dark Green, Navy, Olive.

Purple can be dyed Brown, Claret, Green, Navy, Olive, Prune.

Rose can be dyed any ordinary colour.

Ruby can be dyed Brown, Claret, Dark Mauve, Dark Green, Navy, Olive,
Prune.

Scarlet can be dyed Brown, Crimson, Dark Green, Maroon, Navy, Olive,
Ruby, Terra Cotta.

Slate and Straw can be dyed any ordinary colour, but ought to be
made darker shades, as they do not re-dye satisfactorily.

Terra Cotta can be dyed Brown, Claret, Dark Green, Navy, Olive,
Prune.

NOTE.--DRAB, FAWN, GREY, SLATE and STRAW do not re-dye
satisfactorily, as they require to be a much darker shade to hide
fades. Re-dyed goods have generally to be made a darker shade,
and unless instructed to the contrary Harrods assume they have
permission to do this.

At Harrods there is a wonderful series of separate Service
Departments run for the convenience of clients. These undertake the
insurance of life, property and servants, buy, sell or let houses
and estates, buy or sell stocks and shares, let safes in which
to keep valuables, let out on hire such useful things as pianos,
cutlery, plate, linen, &c. Harrods will at the shortest notice
supply everything for social functions and carry same through
without trouble to the hostess. One can book seats at the Theatres,
secure tickets for railway journeys, book sea passages, despatch
household and other property to any part of the world. You can get
your hair dressed, hire a carriage or motor car, lunch or dine on
the premises, enjoy the club and reading room, join an up-to-date
library, advertise in any paper, warehouse your furniture and
effects, store furs, tapestries, etc., in a specially constructed
cold-air chamber, and open a banking account.


 BANKING DEPARTMENT

 SITUATED IN HARRODS’ ROYAL EXCHANGE.

CURRENT ACCOUNTS--Current Accounts are opened for Shareholders and
Customers or friends introduced by them.

Interest at the rate of 2½ per cent. per annum free of Income Tax is
allowed upon the minimum monthly balance, provided it is not under
£20, and such interest is credited annually in the first week in
January.

No Commission charged for keeping Accounts, but the opening lodgment
must not be under £20, nor the minimum balance less than £10.

Cheques are made up in books of 30, 60, 100, and 120, and will be
charged to clients at the actual cost of stamps--viz.:-- 2/6, 5/0,
8/4, and 10/- respectively.

Pass Books will be made up weekly or otherwise to suit clients, but
in all cases should be returned every quarter-day for comparison
with the Ledgers.

DEPOSIT ACCOUNTS.--Money is received on deposit in sums of not
less than £5, nor more than £300, subject to seven days’ notice of
withdrawal.

Interest free of Income Tax is allowed from date of deposit to date
upon which withdrawal notice expires, and is paid half-yearly--viz.,
30th June and 31st December.

The Directors reserve to themselves the power to return deposits or
change the rate of interest upon giving one month’s notice.

Any change of address should be notified to the Manager of the
Banking Department to ensure the interest being remitted direct.

Deposit Accounts may not be drawn upon by Cheque; but at any time a
sum may be transferred to Current Account upon receipt of Deposit
Note with the necessary instructions written thereon, duly signed by
the Depositor.

Country or other drafts will be received and placed to credit of
account when realised, without charge for clearing.

Dividends, Annuities, Pensions, etc., received and placed to credit
of account or remitted as may be arranged.

Circular Notes and Letters of Credit obtained.

BILLS FOR COLLECTION.--The collection of Bills on London and
Provinces, either Clean or Documentary, is undertaken on the
following terms:--

  A Commission of 1¼ per centum, which covers all ordinary expenses
  of collection and remission, but a Minimum of Two Shillings and
  Sixpence is charged on small Bills of £10 and under.

  Bill Stamps, Notarial Expenses, &c., extra if incurred.

  Instructions should accompany Drafts as to procedure in case of
  non-payment.

STOCKS AND SHARES.--For the convenience of Shareholders and
Customers the Directors have arranged for the Manager of this
Department to afford all necessary information as to prices of
Shares to intending Buyers or Sellers, and to transact business on
their behalf with the Company’s Brokers, the terms for which will be
forwarded on application to the Manager of the Department.

_Remittances may be made by Cheque, Bank Notes, Postal Orders, or
Coin, but should in all cases be registered._

A personal interview is desirable in the opening of an account, but
this formula may be dispensed with by filling up the form provided
for the convenience of Customers residing at a distance from the
Stores, which will be forwarded on application.

_Banking Hours: Nine to Six. Saturdays: Nine to One._

DETAILED INVENTORIES AND VALUATIONS of the whole contents of TOWN
AND COUNTRY HOUSES

An admitted defect of the present system of Fire Insurance is the
possibility that the Insurer may be called upon in the event of loss
occurring from either Fire or Burglary _to produce evidence of the
existence and Proof of the Value_ of all or any article destroyed.
The difficulty of so doing after a fire is obvious.

TO GUARD YOURSELF AGAINST SERIOUS LOSS arm yourself with a detailed
Inventory and Valuation _beforehand_.

A SPECIAL POLICY, can be issued when a value has been placed upon
the contents of the whole house by us.

For further details apply to THE HEAD VALUER, HARRODS LTD.,
Valuation and Estate Office.

[Illustration: HARRODS SAFE DEPOSIT]

AS SAFE AS THE BANK OF ENGLAND

[Illustration: ENTRANCE TO HARRODS’ SAFE DEPOSIT]

Harrods’ Safe Deposit--isolated from the outside world--is
absolutely secure against Burglary, Fire, Explosives, or Damp.

Never a day passes but some daring burglary is committed--someone’s
much valued treasures or heirlooms are stolen; insurance cannot
replace these nor cover their loss when sentimental reasons prevail.

Harrods are continually receiving letters from Renters in their Safe
Deposit, whose houses have been broken into. Yet they are happily
congratulating themselves because their valuables are in safe
keeping at Harrods’.

THE most up-to-date Safety Vault in the World. It contains every
appliance of mechanical ingenuity known to science, invented to
outwit the most accomplished safe breaker, in addition to its
absolute security from Fire, Explosives and Damp. Over 30,000 boxes,
plate chests, etc., have been collected and delivered to customers
during the last 12 years. The list of Renters includes, among other
notabilities, an Egyptian Princess, whose deposit in Jewellery was
valued at over £600,000.

Ratner’s Patent Compo Steel, which is used throughout, has resisted
the most perfect drill manufactured. Even if the Stores were
consumed by flames the Safe Deposit Vaults and contents would be
uninjured.

The main doors guarding the Safes and Strong Rooms have upon them,
in addition to three unpickable and gunpowder-proof locks, Time or
Clock Locks, so that when the Deposit is closed at night, under no
circumstances can the doors be opened again until business hours
next morning (not even by those in possession of the keys), or such
other time as the clocks may be set for by the order of the Managing
Director to cover Sundays and Holidays.

What The Standard says about HARRODS’ SAFE DEPOSIT

“It is satisfactory to note that the steps taken by the well-known
West End establishment, Harrods, to meet this requirement in their
section of the metropolis has met with well-merited success. ‘It is
difficult to estimate the amount of wealth in our keeping,’ said
the manager of their Safe Deposit Department. ‘The depositors do
not always take us into their confidence, but we learn something
occasionally through the inquiries of the insurance companies.
During the trouble in Portugal we had a dress-box brought here which
was filled with gold plate. Now and again a depositor will display
the contents of a chest. During the Coronation festivities this
happened in the case of the sister of the Khedive of Egypt, who
showed me and allowed me to handle some of the finest pearls in the
world, amongst which were specimens as large as pigeons’ eggs. She
showed me, amongst other things, the black pearls presented to her
by the late King Edward on his return from India. Again, just before
the Russo-Japanese war Prince David Beboutoff, when negotiating
a loan in this country, deposited here share certificates worth
close on a million of money. This was only one deposit out of
thousands which take place every year. We have had the title deeds,
securities, and other property lodged here of fifty people who have
died and whose property has been valued for probate at upwards of
£5,000,000.’”

HARRODS’ MODEL DEPOSIT

“An inspection of Messrs. Harrods’ Safe Deposit Department is a
revelation of fire and burglar resisting devices. The most cunning
thief might as well try to wrest valuable mineral from the moon
as steal gold from these vaults, which are a maze of time-locks,
steel doors, steel and wrought iron bars, joists, and floors,
whilst, outside, the arrangements for swamping the outer skin of the
premises with water are perfect. These stores are distinguished as
being the first in this or any other country to add to their other
conveniences a Safe Deposit Department.”

increases greatly the value of the Catalogue.

intellectual classes in England are reading, this Catalogue is a
document of high literary interest. The advantages of opening and

¶ It ensures your every desire receiving the earnest attention

A SOCIAL PILOT.

The latest scheme devised by Harrods to pilot their patrons through
the quicksand of social existence will certainly come as a boon
and a blessing to a great many people who realise the endless
perplexities, anxieties, and those thousand and one worrying details
which are attendant upon the honour of presentation at their
Majesties’ Court.

Indeed, more than half the pleasure of such a command is marred for
a great many people owing to the trouble of getting ready. This is
especially true in the case of first presentations or the attendance
of Americans or Colonials, who, returning home after many years’
sojourn abroad, are utterly perplexed as to all those unwritten
laws that hedge about the ceremony of making their bow to their
Sovereign. For explicit and precise as the rules and regulations
issued by the Lord Chamberlain are, they by no means relieve the
novice of all trouble, responsibility, and care in the matter.

THE SARTORIAL PICK OF EUROPE.

This, however, is exactly what Harrods is prepared to do. Not only
do they undertake to supply all the necessary outfit, from a Court
dress and regulation train to the necessary feathers and veil, but
they are further prepared to save one all trouble concerning those
maddening minor details that entail more care and anxiety than
everything else put together. With the new system there are no more
distracted pursuits of gloves that must be of exactly the correct
tint, no more wearying discussions as to the type of shoe to be
worn. Under Harrods’ management all is thought out and considered,
weighed and decided; one’s own taste being consulted in the first
instance when every possible alternative is placed before one.
Indeed, with one interview it is quite possible to end all further
discussion and trouble. So it is with everything else; for here not
only is everything supplied at a moderate cost, but one can take
one’s choice from a stock that is larger than any other in London,
and one that literally does represent the sartorial pick of Europe
gathered together and displayed under one roof.

THE ALL-IMPORTANT COURT COIFFURE.

Even in the matter of coiffure one is equally well catered for. For
Harrods have an expert staff of hairdressers who are thoroughly
versed in the mysteries of Court coiffure and who know to a nicety
all that there is to be known concerning the manipulation of hair
to suit the latest style of arranging the regulation plumes and
veil--a detail of utmost importance that may, and often does, make
or mar the whole general effect of many a Court toilette, for a
badly-dressed head is even more damaging than a badly-fitting dress
on such occasions.

Court coiffures are dressed at Harrods at 7/6 per head.

SPECIALLY DESIGNED COURT BOUQUETS.

In the same way Harrods will supply the _débutante_ with the
correct type of bouquet needed for this all-important occasion. For
bouquets, like every other detail connected with personal adornment,
call for individual care and attention nowadays. Ordering from
Harrods one may be satisfied that this is as carefully dealt with in
detail as everything else, and the result will be not only a bouquet
suitable for the occasion, but one that has been specially designed
with an eye to what is becoming to the height, the figure, and the
frock of the lady who orders it.

Court bouquets at Harrods are supplied from 10/6 upward.

MOTOR-CARS AND FOOTMEN AT EVERYONE’s COMMAND.

Even when all these details have been arranged, Harrods is still
ready to supply luxuriously appointed motor-cars and landaulettes,
which are sent out in the care of experienced chauffeurs and footmen
who thoroughly understand the ropes, and who are au fait with the
many regulations that govern the setting down and taking up of their
Majesties’ guests. On occasion like this it is no small comfort to
be able to engage footmen who have season after season performed the
same duties, so that there is no fear of confusion, mistakes, or any
unnecessary delays.

Harrods’ motor-car hire tariff will be sent to anyone on
application. For one evening’s hire to attend a Court the cost is 2½
gns. and 3 gns.

THE UBIQUITOUS PORTRAIT.

Even in the case of the ubiquitous souvenir portrait of the great
occasion Harrods is ready to render valuable assistance. They
have a specially fitted-up studio and expert photographers on the
premises who make a _spécialité_ of this style of portraiture. In
this particular, customers who avail themselves of Harrods’ complete
Court catering will be able to save themselves a good deal of
trouble and fatigue, as it is an easy matter to arrange to pay a
visit to Harrods’ Studio before one’s finery is finally sent home,
so avoiding the fatigue of visiting a photographer’s after the Court
is over, when one is tired out and consequently looking anything but
at the best advantage.

Harrods’ charges for portraits: Boudoir size, £1 13s. for 6 copies;
Panel size, £2 12s. 6d. for 6 copies.

MENTAL AND FINANCIAL ECONOMY.

The secret of the success of this complete Court catering lies
in the thoroughness with which it is carried out from beginning
to end. For, from the moment when the expert designers are first
consulted about one’s dress, to the concluding visit to the
photographer, everything is made easy and pleasant, all the burden
and responsibility being lifted from one’s own shoulders to that of
experts specially trained in the many details that contribute to the
success of the whole. Moreover, the plan makes for economy in every
direction--economy of time, since the arrangements can be made under
one roof and at one visit; economy of expense, since we know that
whatever be decided upon will be correct and will necessitate no
further outlay at the last moment, and, above all, economy of mental
wear and tear. Indeed, so easy is it all that one may be forgiven
tending toward a comfortable laziness in regard to social duties.
For Harrods’ service makes it so simple to avoid unnecessary social
fatigue and difficulties that it is not surprising to find every
year more and more folk are availing themselves of the facilities
which are offered to them.

How Harrods have developed Shopping by Telephone

SINCE its inception Harrods’ Telephone Order Office has proved
an unqualified success. Being efficiently organised as a special
department, all orders are carefully taken, and the tantalising
treatment often meted out to orders by telephone, where they are
dealt with in haphazard manner, is entirely avoided.

The staff of Order Clerks is a specially trained force always in
attendance--Day and Night--to attend to customers’ enquiries and
orders.

Orders ’phoned during business hours are promptly executed and
dispatched, and those received after business hours are sent by the
early morning delivery vans and mails next day.

Customers’ or Harrods’ stables, on a yearly contract, new carriages

No attempt has been made to mark up bold text, or the many changes
to character font sizes from the original.

The following inserted ERRATUM slip on page 826 has been applied...
 "The illustration of the Welte-Mignon should be the Steinway-Welte
  and vice versa"

On page 833 the original page was trimmed at the right causing a partial
loss of prices, this is noted within the text.

The index of departments lists page 1442 as the start of the
FUNERAL DEPARTMENT, but the original omits any such heading, so this
heading has been added as a typographical error.

The following typographical errors are corrected without specific mention.
 Missing full stops on abbreviated words
 Missing quotation marks
 Missing / (shilling/pence separator)

The original focal ratios i.e. ƒ/6·8 appeared in a variety formats,
some using the florin symbol ƒ others with a capital F, some with
the decimal point being superscript, or as period. All have all
been normalized to ƒ and · mid-dot.

Gun bores are marked . or · inconsistently across different pages
changed all to · mid-dot.

Accents have been left as in the original, but ligatures if used
within a word are standardized without specific mention.
